--- name: android-device-lab description: Safe analysis of Android phones and tablets via adb/fastboot, firmware triage, and planning or executing postmarketOS / Linux ports and installs. Use whenever the user mentions adb, fastboot, bootloader unlock, identifying an Android device (SoC, partitions, A/B, Treble, dynamic partitions), firmware/OTA/factory images, boot.img, vendor_boot, dtb, vendor kernel, postmarketOS, pmbootstrap, mainline Linux on a phone or tablet, or flashing a custom OS, even if they do not say "skill". Enforces read-only-first, backup-before-write and explicit confirmation before anything destructive. license: MIT compatibility: opencode (also works as a Claude-style skill). Needs adb and fastboot (android-platform-tools); optional pmbootstrap, avbtool, unpack_bootimg, payload-dumper-go, simg2img, lpunpack, fsck.erofs, dtc, binwalk. scripts/setup-host.sh installs them. metadata: domain: android-hardware risk: high-when-flashing --- # Android Device Lab Analyse Android phones/tablets, assess whether Linux / postmarketOS can run on them, prepare ports, and flash only when every safety gate has passed. Reply in the language of the user. Keep commands and file names in English. Skill id in opencode is the directory name (`android-device-lab`); the frontmatter `name` is only a display label. ## Prime directives 1. **Read-only first.** Always start with `scripts/device-info.sh`. Do not write to the device until the report exists and the user has read it. 2. **One device, one serial.** If more than one device is connected, stop and ask which serial. Always use `adb -s ` / `fastboot -s ` once chosen. 3. **Never improvise destructive commands.** Anything in Tier 2 or 3 (see below) requires: backup verified, exact command shown, user confirmation in this conversation. Never chain it with `&&` to other actions. 4. **Prefer non-persistent tests.** Use `fastboot boot ` (RAM only) before `fastboot flash`. If the target does not support it, say so and explain the added risk. 5. **Never touch low-level partitions** (bootloader, aboot/abl/xbl, sbl, tz, modem/radio, preloader, persist, efs, nvram/nvdata, frp, rpmb) unless the user explicitly asks, understands that this can hard-brick the device, and a recovery path (EDL, BROM, Odin download mode, etc.) is confirmed for that exact model. 6. **Treat firmware as untrusted.** Extract into a work directory, never execute or mount-as-root anything from it, verify hashes against the vendor source when available. 7. **Privacy.** Do not print or store IMEI, serial in clear, MAC addresses, account names. The scripts redact these; keep it that way in reports. Partition backups contain unique identifiers: keep them local, never commit or upload them. 8. **Say what you don't know.** If a model/SoC is not in the postmarketOS device list or the unlock status is unclear, say so instead of guessing. 9. **Verify, never assume.** Device support, unlock policy and rollback indexes change; check the current wiki/vendor documentation instead of relying on memory. 10. **The user keeps ownership of their phone.** This skill assists the owner of a device they own. Never assist with FRP/activation-lock bypass, IMEI/serial rewriting, anti-theft circumvention or locked-carrier defeat. ## Safety tiers | Tier | Meaning | Examples | Rule | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | Read-only | `adb devices`, `adb shell getprop`, `fastboot getvar`, reading files, offline firmware analysis | Run freely | | 1 | Reversible, device-side or host-side state | `adb reboot`, `adb pull`, `adb install`, `fastboot boot`, `adb shell settings`, installing host packages | Tell the user what you are doing | | 2 | Modifies persistent storage or security state | `fastboot flash boot/recovery/vbmeta/system`, `fastboot flashing unlock`, `adb sideload`, `fastboot set_active` | Backup + exact command + explicit confirmation | | 3 | Can brick or wipe irrecoverably | `fastboot erase`, `fastboot format`, `flashing lock` with custom OS, flashing bootloader/modem/persist, `dd of=/dev/block/*`, anti-rollback bumps | Refuse by default; only with explicit, informed override | Full rules and per-vendor pitfalls: `references/safety.md`. ## Workflow ### 0. Prepare the host (Tier 1 on the PC, never on the phone) ```bash bash scripts/setup-host.sh --check # what is missing (read-only) bash scripts/setup-host.sh --minimal # adb + fastboot bash scripts/setup-host.sh --full # + dtc, lz4, avbtool, payload-dumper-go, simg2img, # lpunpack, pmbootstrap, mtkclient ``` The script only installs what is missing, never removes or downgrades packages, and prints the sha256 of every binary it downloads. Run `--dry-run` first if the user wants to see the plan. If the machine is locked down, fall back to manual install using `references/tooling.md`. ### 1. Recon (Tier 0) ```bash bash scripts/device-info.sh ./recon- # adb mode bash scripts/device-info.sh ./recon- --fastboot # bootloader mode bash scripts/device-info.sh --list # what is attached ``` Read `summary.md` and the raw files. Report: manufacturer, model, codename, SoC/platform, Android version and security patch, bootloader lock state, verified boot state, A/B or not, dynamic partitions, Treble, kernel version, partition layout, display, battery. Every claim in the report must be traceable to a file in the recon directory. ### 2. Feasibility assessment - Check the postmarketOS wiki device list for the codename (`references/ecosystem.md`): classify as already supported (community/main/testing), supported on a close sibling (same SoC/board), or no port. - Check whether the bootloader can be unlocked (vendor policy, waiting periods, carrier locks, OEM unlock toggle, data wipe on unlock, warranty/Knox/eFuse effects). - Check SoC tier: Qualcomm (mainline support varies; EDL recovery often available), MediaTek (preloader/BROM, vendor kernels common), Exynos/Unisoc/Rockchip/Allwinner (case by case). - Check anti-rollback (`fastboot getvar anti`, vbmeta rollback index) before proposing any flash. - Give the user a go/no-go with risks before proposing any write. ### 3. Backup gate (Tier 1 → required before Tier 2) ```bash bash scripts/backup-partitions.sh --list # what exists on this device bash scripts/backup-partitions.sh --group core --plan bash scripts/backup-partitions.sh --group all --yes # pulls + sha256 + manifest ``` `core` covers boot-like and vbmeta partitions; `all` adds the device-unique calibration partitions (persist, efs, modemst, nvdata, proinfo, protect_*). These hold the unique IMEI/Wi-Fi/sensor calibration and exist in **no** firmware download, so a factory reflash does not restore them. The script reads only; it never writes a partition. If the device is not rooted, say so and offer the alternatives (`adb root` on userdebug builds, a custom recovery, or accepting the risk explicitly). Also remind the user to copy their own data (photos, messages, authenticator seeds) - `adb backup` is deprecated and unreliable. Do not proceed to Tier 2 without a verified backup of at least boot + the calibration partitions, or an explicit "I accept the risk". ### 4. Firmware analysis (offline, Tier 0 on the host) ```bash bash scripts/firmware-triage.sh ./fw- ``` Details and tool usage: `references/firmware-analysis.md`. Produce: manifest with hashes, image types, AVB/vbmeta info, boot header (kernel cmdline, page size, header version, dtb), partition scheme (super/dynamic), kernel version string, device tree model/compatible. The bundled parser (`scripts/lib/bootimg.py`) reads boot/vendor_boot/init_boot headers with no extra dependency; `unpack_bootimg` and `pmbootstrap bootimg_analyze` add detail when installed. ### 5. Install path - **A. Existing postmarketOS port**: follow `references/pmos-porting.md` section A. Use `pmbootstrap` for build and flash; test with `pmbootstrap flasher boot` (or `fastboot boot`) first. - **B. New port**: follow `references/pmos-porting.md` section B and `references/porting-playbook.md`. Start from the stock boot image analysis, a downstream vendor kernel, and a `deviceinfo`; get "boots to initramfs with USB networking/telnet" first, then display, touch, storage, Wi-Fi, etc. Track the status per subsystem. - **C. Generic Linux (Droidian, UBports, Halium, chroot/proot)**: lower risk options on stock Android. Offer them as alternatives when a native port is too risky. ### 6. Flash gate Before every Tier 2 command, print this checklist and wait for "yes": ``` Device: / / serial hash Mode: fastboot | recovery | download Bootloader: unlocked? yes/no Backup: (sha256 verified) Image: sha256 <...> Command: Effect: Recovery path: ``` One command per confirmation. No `&&` chains. If the user asks for a Tier 3 action, restate the brick risk and the recovery path, and require an explicit override; if there is no confirmed recovery path for that exact model, refuse. ### 7. Report Write `REPORT.md` in the work directory (template: `references/report-template.md`): device facts, evidence (file references), feasibility verdict, steps taken with exact commands, backups with hashes, open issues, and a clear separation of **observed** / **documented** / **assumed** facts. ## Output style Short, factual. Distinguish **observed** (from the device/firmware), **documented** (wiki/vendor), and **assumed** (your inference). Never present an assumption as a fact. Use tables for device facts and subsystem status. Keep the exact commands you ran. ## Bundled resources - `scripts/install.sh`: install the skill into opencode and merge the permission rules. - `scripts/setup-host.sh`: install and verify the host toolchain. - `scripts/device-info.sh`: read-only recon over adb/fastboot with redaction. - `scripts/firmware-triage.sh`: safe offline unpack and inventory of firmware. - `scripts/backup-partitions.sh`: read-only backup of device-unique partitions with hashes. - `scripts/lib/bootimg.py`: dependency-free Android boot image header parser. - `scripts/lint.sh`: repository self-check (run before committing changes). - `references/safety.md`: tiers, vendor-specific brick risks, recovery modes. - `references/pmos-porting.md`: postmarketOS flow for existing and new ports. - `references/porting-playbook.md`: expert bring-up order, subsystem matrix, failure table. - `references/kernel-and-dts.md`: kernel, device tree and defconfig workflow. - `references/firmware-analysis.md`: formats, tools, what to extract. - `references/tooling.md`: what each tool does and how to install it. - `references/ecosystem.md`: authoritative upstream sources (wiki, DTS, kernels, specs). - `references/report-template.md`: REPORT.md skeleton. - `assets/opencode.permissions.example.json`: opencode V2 permission rules enforcing the tiers. - `assets/opencode.permissions.v1.example.json`: same rules for opencode V1.

# android-device-lab

An [opencode](https://opencode.ai) skill for **safe analysis of Android phones and
tablets** and for **porting them to Linux / postmarketOS**.

It gives an agent the workflow, the tooling and the guard rails to:

- identify a device (SoC, codename, partitions, A/B, Treble, dynamic partitions),
  read-only, over `adb` or `fastboot`;
- triage firmware offline (factory images, OTA payloads, vendor tarballs) without
  executing anything from them;
- judge whether a bootloader can be unlocked and whether a postmarketOS port is
  realistic;
- prepare a port (kernel, device tree, `deviceinfo`, initramfs bring-up) and flash
  only when every safety gate has passed.

Everything destructive is behind a gate: read-only first, verified backup before any
write, the exact command shown before it runs, and an explicit confirmation.

## Install

### The easy way (one command)

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lordpietre/android-device-lab/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

That does everything:

1. installs the skill into `~/.config/opencode/skills/android-device-lab`;
2. merges the safety permission rules into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
   (backing your config up to `opencode.json.bak` first);
3. prints the next steps.

Restart opencode and the skill is ready. It is also usable right away with
`@android-device-lab` or from the skill picker.

Other options:

```bash
# project-local instead of global
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lordpietre/android-device-lab/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --project

# skip the opencode.json merge
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lordpietre/android-device-lab/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --no-permissions

# remove it again
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lordpietre/android-device-lab/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --uninstall
```

### Manual

The skill id is the directory name, so the folder has to be called `android-device-lab`.

```bash
# global (recommended)
git clone https://github.com/lordpietre/android-device-lab.git ~/.config/opencode/skills/android-device-lab

# project-local
git clone https://github.com/lordpietre/android-device-lab.git .opencode/skills/android-device-lab
```

opencode also reads `~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/` and
`.agents/skills/`, so the same folder works with the Claude-style layout.

### Permissions (optional, the installer does it for you)

`assets/opencode.permissions.example.json` (opencode V2) or
`assets/opencode.permissions.v1.example.json` (opencode V1) contain the rules that
allow the read-only commands, ask before any write to a device, and deny the
operations that can hard-brick a phone. Merge the `permissions` array into your
`opencode.json(c)`.

> The last matching rule wins, so the broad `"*": "ask"` rule comes first and the
> specific rules follow it.

## Host requirements

`bash scripts/setup-host.sh --check` reports what is missing.

| Tool | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `adb`, `fastboot` | yes | device access |
| `python3` | yes | bundled boot image parser |
| `dtc`, `lz4`, `unzip`, `7z`, `strings`, `file` | recommended | firmware analysis |
| `avbtool`, `payload-dumper-go`, `simg2img`, `lpunpack`, `unpack_bootimg` | optional | deeper firmware analysis |
| `pmbootstrap`, `git`, `curl` | optional | building and flashing postmarketOS |

```bash
bash scripts/setup-host.sh --minimal   # adb + fastboot
bash scripts/setup-host.sh --full      # the full toolchain (never removes or downgrades)
```

## Usage

```bash
# 1. read-only reconnaissance
bash scripts/device-info.sh ./recon-<codename>
bash scripts/device-info.sh ./recon-<codename> --fastboot   # bootloader mode

# 2. offline firmware triage
bash scripts/firmware-triage.sh firmware.zip ./fw-<name>

# 3. back up the device-unique partitions (read-only on the phone)
bash scripts/backup-partitions.sh --list
bash scripts/backup-partitions.sh --group all --yes

# 4. inspect a boot image without any extra dependency
python3 scripts/lib/bootimg.py info boot.img
```

Then ask opencode: *"analyze this phone with android-device-lab"*, *"can this device
run postmarketOS?"*, *"prepare a port for <codename>"*.

## Safety model

| Tier | Meaning | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Read-only (recon, `getvar`, offline firmware analysis) | run freely |
| 1 | Reversible (reboot, pull, RAM boot, host installs) | say what you are doing |
| 2 | Persistent writes (`fastboot flash`, unlock, sideload) | backup + exact command + confirmation |
| 3 | Irreversible (erase, format, bootloader/modem/persist, re-lock) | refused unless explicitly overridden |

Hard rules: never write to the device before the recon report exists, never touch
bootloader/modem/persist/efs/nvram partitions, never flash without a verified
backup, never bypass FRP/activation locks or modify IMEI, and never present an
assumption as a fact.

## Repository layout

```
android-device-lab/
├── SKILL.md                        the skill itself
├── scripts/
│   ├── install.sh                   one-command installer (skill + permissions)
│   ├── setup-host.sh                install/verify the host toolchain
│   ├── device-info.sh              read-only recon (adb / fastboot)
```

# Firmware analysis

Everything in this file happens **offline, on the host, read-only**. Nothing is
executed, installed or mounted from the firmware.

## Formats
| Source | Container | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| Pixel / AOSP factory images | zip with images + flash-all | unzip, fastboot |
| A/B OTA | zip with `payload.bin` | payload-dumper-go |
| Samsung | AP/BL/CP/CSC `.tar.md5` (+ lz4) | tar, lz4 |
| Qualcomm full | `rawprogram*.xml`, `patch*.xml`, firehose `.mbn` | read XML to get partition map |
| MediaTek | scatter file + images | scatter.txt gives partition map |
| Sparse images | `system.img` etc. | simg2img |
| Dynamic partitions | `super.img` | lpunpack |
| Filesystems | ext4 / EROFS / f2fs | `debugfs -R`, `fsck.erofs --extract`, 7z; read-only, never run binaries |

## One-shot triage

```bash
bash scripts/firmware-triage.sh <firmware> ./fw-<name>
```

It extracts the container, unpacks `payload.bin` and `super.img` when the tools are
available, identifies every image by magic bytes, parses the boot headers, dumps the
AVB information and writes `manifest.md` with hashes and sizes.

## What to extract
- Boot images: header version, kernel cmdline, page size, offsets, dtb (`unpack_bootimg`, `pmbootstrap bootimg_analyze`, or the bundled `scripts/lib/bootimg.py`).
- Kernel version: `strings boot.img | grep 'Linux version'`; decompress `kernel` if needed (gzip/lz4) and re-run strings.
- Device tree: `dtc -I dtb -O dts` then check `model`, `compatible`, panel nodes, touch IC, regulators.
- vbmeta: `avbtool info_image` for rollback index, flags and chained partitions.
- Partition map: from `/dev/block/by-name` (device) or scatter/rawprogram (firmware).
- Vendor blobs: list only (`ls`), identify GPU/Wi-Fi/modem firmware names; do not redistribute them.

## Boot image headers in practice

```bash
python3 scripts/lib/bootimg.py info boot.img            # header, cmdline, page size, sizes
python3 scripts/lib/bootimg.py extract boot.img ./out     # kernel / ramdisk / dtb
python3 scripts/lib/bootimg.py dts boot.img               # dtb model + compatible
```

The parser understands the classic layout (v0-v3) and the v4 layout (Android 12+),
plus `vendor_boot`. It prints what it could not determine instead of guessing.

Key fields and what they break when wrong:

| Field | Breaks when wrong |
|---|---|
| `header_version` | the bootloader refuses or mis-parses the image |
| `page_size` | image is read at the wrong offsets (wrong kernel, empty screen) |
| `cmdline` (`root=`, `console=`, `androidboot.*`) | wrong rootfs, no console, no USB gadget |
| `dtb` | wrong panel/touch/regulators, black screen |
| `os_version` | the bootloader may reject the image on some devices |

## Super / dynamic partitions

```bash
lpunlock super.img ./unpacked/      # logical partitions
simg2img system.img system.raw.img   # sparse -> raw
fsck.erofs --extract=./erofs system.img   # EROFS, read-only
```

## Integrity and trust
- Compare SHA256 with the vendor's published value.
- Be suspicious of repacked/unsigned firmware from forums; analyse in a VM or container without network and never run extracted binaries.
- Keep a manifest: file name, hash, source URL, date.

## What the manifest must contain
File name, size, sha256, detected type, boot header fields, kernel version string,
dtb model/compatible, AVB rollback index and flags, partition map source, and a note
of which tools were missing (so a follow-up run can fill the gaps).

# Kernel and device tree workflow

Everything needed to turn a stock Android boot image into a bootable mainline Linux.

## 1. Identify the kernel you are replacing

From the recon (`scripts/device-info.sh`):

```bash
adb shell uname -a
adb shell cat /proc/version
adb shell cat /proc/cmdline
```

- `Linux version 4.4.302-perf+ ...` → the vendor kernel is 4.4 (2016-era). Mainline
  support for that SoC may exist or may not.
- `Linux version 5.10.177-android13-8-...` → a recent GKI/vendor kernel, mainline is
  usually closer.
- `Hardware : Qualcomm Technologies, Inc SM6375` in `/proc/cpuinfo` → the SoC codename
  is what you need, not the marketing name.

Map the marketing name to the SoC codename (`SM6375`, `MSM8998`, `MT6781`, `Exynos
2100`, ...) before looking for DTS files.

## 2. Get the device tree

### From the stock boot image

```bash
bash scripts/firmware-triage.sh boot.img ./fw-boot
python3 scripts/lib/bootimg.py extract boot.img ./fw-boot/unpacked   # vendor_boot/init_boot too
dtc -I dtb -O dts -o vendor.dts fw-boot/unpacked/boot.dtb
```

`bootimg.py info` prints the header (cmdline, page size, header version, dtb size)
without any extra tool.

For `vendor_boot` images the board DTB is usually appended to the vendor ramdisk
(`boot.img`/`vendor_boot.img` may not contain the DTB at all on Treble devices).

### From the kernel source

- Mainline: `arch/arm64/boot/dts/<vendor>/` in the Linux tree. Look for the board
  file, not just the SoC file: `<vendor>/<soc>.dtsi` + `<vendor>/<board>.dts`.
- Vendor (GPL release, mandatory by the GPL): the vendor's kernel source tarball,
  `arch/arm64/boot/dts/`.

### Converting a vendor DTB to a source DTS

```bash
dtc -I dtb -O dts -o vendor.dts vendor.dtb        # decompile
dtc -I dts -O dtb -o vendor-clean.dtb vendor.dts  # recompile (may warn)
```

Then hand-edit: fix `model`/`compatible`, drop vendor-specific nodes, and add the
mainline driver bindings the panel/touch/regulator need. Keep the decompiled file
as a reference, not as a build input.

Useful helpers: `fdtget`, `fdtdump` (device-tree-compiler package), `dtdiff`.

## 3. Choose the kernel base

| Base | When |
|---|---|
| Mainline (`torvalds/linux`) | long term, cleanest, needs DTS + driver work |
| postmarketOS kernel fork | pmOS-specific patches (initramfs, USB gadget) already applied |
| Vendor downstream kernel | fastest to first boot; huge diff, rarely upstreamable |

postmarketOS ports normally use the pmOS kernel fork with per-device patches in
`linux-<vendor>-<codename>`. Say explicitly which base you chose and why.

## 4. Kernel configuration

Minimum set for a phone/tablet bring-up:

```
CONFIG_USB_GADGET=y
CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS=y
CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_FS=y
CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_RNDIS=y
CONFIG_USB_OTG=y
CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD=y
CONFIG_EXT4_FS=y
CONFIG_SCSI=y / CONFIG_UFS=y / CONFIG_MMC=y      (storage)
CONFIG_DRM=y + CONFIG_DRM_PANEL_*=y              (display)
CONFIG_TOUCHSCREEN_*=y                           (touch)
CONFIG_SND_SOC=y                                 (audio)
CONFIG_WLAN_VENDOR_* / CONFIG_WLAN=y             (wifi)
```

Workflow with pmbootstrap:

```bash
pmbootstrap kconfig merge     # merge the device config with the kernel defaults
pmbootstrap kconfig check      # verify the merged config is valid
pmbootstrap linux              # build the kernel inside the chroot
```

Keep the config in the kernel package directory (`config` file or a fragment
applied by the APKBUILD) so the build is reproducible.

## 5. Build a boot image

The boot image is: header + kernel + ramdisk + (dtb) + (footer for v1-v3).

- `deviceinfo_generate_bootimg: true` lets pmbootstrap build the image from
  `deviceinfo` (cmdline, page size, header version, dtb).
- Manual build with `mkbootimg`:
  ```bash
  mkbootimg --header_version 4 --kernel Image --ramdisk initramfs \
            --cmdline "..." --output boot.img
  ```
- The bundled `scripts/lib/bootimg.py` can inspect what you produced, and
  `unpack_bootimg --format=mkbootimg` gives the full split.

Header versions: v0-v3 (classic, 32-bit era layout) vs v4 (Android 12+, 64-bit
layout with a 1536-byte cmdline). Mismatching the header version of the original
image is a classic "it worked with the vendor kernel but not with mine" bug.

## 6. DTB in the image, or DTB from the bootloader?

Some devices pass the DTB in the boot image, others expect the bootloader to
append it. The stock header tells you which: `dt_size`/`dtb_size` non-zero means
the DTB travels inside the image. If the original image has no DTB, the board DTB
must be loaded by the bootloader (or flashed to `dtbo`) and referenced by
`androidboot.dtb`/partition name.

## 7. Patches and hygiene

- One patch per driver/bug, with a `Signed-off-by` and a description of the
  hardware it touches.
- Never mix "make it boot" changes with "make it clean" changes.
- Keep a `NOTES.md` in the port directory: what was tried, what failed, and why.
- When the port becomes useful to others, upstream the kernel patches and open a
  pull request against the postmarketOS device list.

## 8. Verification checklist before flashing

```bash
sha256sum boot.img
python3 scripts/lib/bootimg.py info boot.img     # cmdline, page size, header version
fastboot boot boot.img                            # RAM only, no persistence
```

# postmarketOS: existing ports and new ports

Verify current syntax with `pmbootstrap --help` and the postmarketOS wiki; flags and
device categories change between releases. The authoritative guides are listed in
`references/ecosystem.md`.

## A. Device already supported

1. Look up the codename on the wiki device page. Note category (main/community/testing), what works, install method, known bootloader quirks.
2. `pmbootstrap init` (choose vendor, codename, user interface, init options). Work inside the pmbootstrap chroot only.
3. `pmbootstrap install` builds the rootfs and boot image.
4. Non-persistent test first: `pmbootstrap flasher boot` (RAM boot via fastboot). If it works, continue.
5. Persistent flash (Tier 2, confirmation gate): `pmbootstrap flasher flash_kernel` then `pmbootstrap flasher flash_rootfs` (or the method the device page specifies: fastboot, heimdall, sideload, etc.). Mind A/B slot and the partition names on the device page.
6. Recovery: keep stock boot.img backed up; reflash with `fastboot flash boot stock_boot.img` (slot-aware).

### Useful pmbootstrap commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `pmbootstrap init` | create the build environment |
| `pmbootstrap shell` | shell inside the chroot (use it to edit the kernel package) |
| `pmbootstrap info` | show the current configuration |
| `pmbootstrap install` | build rootfs + boot image |
| `pmbootstrap initfs` | build a minimal initramfs for RAM boots |
| `pmbootstrap flasher boot` | RAM boot (fastboot boot), non-persistent |
| `pmbootstrap flasher flash_kernel` | write the kernel/boot image (Tier 2) |
| `pmbootstrap flasher flash_rootfs` | write the rootfs/rootfs image (Tier 2) |
| `pmbootstrap kconfig merge` / `check` | merge and validate the kernel config |
| `pmbootstrap linux` | build the kernel inside the chroot |
| `pmbootstrap log` | show the build log |
| `pmbootstrap clean` | remove the build directory |

### Notes for existing ports
- The wiki page may specify `fastbootd` instead of `fastboot` (dynamic partition
  devices): flashing a partition that lives in `super` requires the userspace
  fastboot (`adb reboot fastboot`).
- If the device is A/B, flash the *other* slot first so the working slot stays
  bootable: `fastboot flash boot --slot _b pmos.img`, verify, then `fastboot set_active _b`.
- Some pages require `fastboot flash vbmeta --disable-verity --disable-verification`
  before a custom kernel boots: that is a Tier 2 action with a real security
  consequence (the verified boot chain no longer protects the device).
- postmarketOS images expect a specific `cmdline` and page size; copying the
  `deviceinfo` from the wiki page is safer than inventing one.

## B. New port

Goal order: (1) boots to initramfs with USB networking, (2) SSH/telnet debug, (3) display + framebuffer, (4) touch, (5) storage, (6) Wi-Fi/BT, (7) GPU, (8) modem/audio/sensors.

1. From recon + firmware triage collect: SoC/platform, kernel version, `cmdline`, boot header version, page size, kernel/ramdisk/dtb offsets, dtb model/compatible, partition names, A/B flag, display panel name, touch IC, Wi-Fi chip.
2. `pmbootstrap bootimg_analyze stock_boot.img` (or `python3 scripts/lib/bootimg.py info stock_boot.img`) to seed `deviceinfo` values (cmdline, offsets, pagesize, header version, dtb).
3. Create packages `device-<vendor>-<codename>` and `linux-<vendor>-<codename>` following the wiki "Porting to a new device" guide. Start from the vendor downstream kernel (download from the vendor's GPL source release; match the exact build) or from mainline, and add a defconfig; use `pmbootstrap kconfig check`.
4. Fill `deviceinfo` (name, manufacturer, codename, arch, chassis, flash method, cmdline, page size, boot image header version, dtb, `deviceinfo_generate_bootimg`, etc.).
5. Iterate with `pmbootstrap flasher boot` (never persistent until it boots). Use serial/USB debug (`pmbootstrap initfs`, telnet to 172.16.42.1 on USB networking).
6. Only after stable RAM boots, flash persistently with the full gate in SKILL.md.
7. Document status per subsystem in the device wiki page format; aim to upstream.

The detailed bring-up order, the failure table and the package layout are in
`references/porting-playbook.md`. The kernel, device tree and config workflow is in
`references/kernel-and-dts.md`.

## Tips
- Mainline is cleaner long-term; downstream is faster to first boot. Say which one you choose and why.
- Keep all kernel config/patch changes in version control.
- If the device lacks `fastboot boot`, use a separate test slot (A/B) or a dedicated recovery partition; if neither exists, state the added risk explicitly.
- Ship the port with a status table: the wiki page format, with each subsystem marked
  working / partial / broken. Honest tables get more upstream contributions than
  optimistic ones.

# Porting playbook

Expert procedure to bring a new phone or tablet to a native Linux/postmarketOS port.
Read `references/kernel-and-dts.md` in parallel: it covers the kernel and device tree work.

## 0. Decide what "port" means

| Goal | Effort | Risk | Typical route |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boot a mainline kernel to initramfs | days–weeks | low (RAM only) | `pmbootstrap` + `fastboot boot` |
| Booting with display + touch | weeks | medium | mainline panel/touch drivers, deviceinfo |
| Daily driver with modem, camera, sensors | months | medium | vendor firmware blobs + community patches |
| Non-persistent install (no persistence, no data wipe) | hours | low–medium | `fastboot boot` of a stock-compatible kernel |
| Persistent install with a custom OS | hours | high | `fastboot flash boot` / `pmbootstrap flasher flash_rootfs` |

Always offer the lowest-risk option that satisfies the user. A RAM boot that works
today beats a persistent install that bricks on Friday.

## 1. Bring-up order (do not skip ahead)

1. **Initramfs + USB networking.** Nothing else matters until you can reach a shell.
2. **SSH/telnet debug access.** `172.16.42.1` over USB RNDIS (postmarketOS initfs
   uses telnet on port 23 in the initfs, SSH on 22 in the installed system).
3. **Display** (panel + backlight + DRM/DRM-KMS driver).
4. **Touch** and **hardware buttons**.
5. **Storage** (UFS/eMMC, filesystem, GPT, fstab, encryption).
6. **Wi-Fi / Bluetooth**.
7. **GPU / 3D** (Panfrost, Freedreno, Mali via Panfrost or Lima).
8. **Audio, sensors, modem, cameras, fingerprint**.

Track it in a status table (see `references/report-template.md`) so progress is visible
and comparable with the wiki page.

## 2. The first boot (RAM only)

```bash
pmbootstrap init                      # vendor, codename, ui, init options
pmbootstrap initfs                    # build a minimal initramfs
apk add --root .initfs --initdb --allow-untrusted -a /path/to/extra.apk   # optional
pmbootstrap flasher boot              # fastboot boot of the initfs image
```

While the initfs runs on the device:

- Serial console: `pmbootstrap flasher --serial`? (pmbootstrap exposes `pmbootstrap
  console`/`pmbootstrap flasher --list`; the usual approach is `fastboot boot` with
  `console=ttyMSM0,115200` in the cmdline and a UART/USB-serial adapter.)
- USB networking: the postmarketOS initfs brings up an RNDIS gadget; on the host run
  `ip addr` and look for `172.16.42.1`, then `telnet 172.16.42.1 23`.
- Logs: `pmbootstrap log`, and `dmesg` on the device.

**Never flash persistently while the RAM boot is not stable.** Every change to the
kernel, cmdline or initfs must be validated with `fastboot boot` first.

## 3. Common failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No USB gadget, no telnet | kernel lacks `CONFIG_USB_CONFIGFS_F_FS` + `CONFIG_USB_GADGET` + RNDIS | enable in the kernel config; check `dmesg` for gadget errors |
| `initramfs panic: unable to mount` | wrong rootfs/partition layout | verify cmdline `root=` against the real GPT layout, and `CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD` |
| Kernel panic very early | wrong dtb / wrong `console=` | try the vendor dtb from the stock boot image; add `earlycon` |
| Black screen but system boots | panel driver missing or wrong `compatible` | check `dmesg` for panel probe, add the matching `drm_panel_` driver, verify the regulator/timing nodes |
| Bootloop after `fastboot flash boot` | A/B slot mismatch, or the flashed image is wrong | flash the other slot (`fastboot flash boot --slot other`), keep the stock image at hand |
| `Verification failed` / orange state | AVB | `fastboot flash vbmeta --disable-verity --disable-verification vbmeta_empty.img` (Tier 2) or boot a signed kernel |
| `dm-verity` / `dm-verity` fails to mount system | verity mismatch after wiping super | flash the whole `super`/`system` from the vendor package, or disable verity |
| Root filesystem not found | wrong `root=`, wrong partition, storage driver missing | dump `cat /proc/partitions` and the GPT from recovery |
| Initramfs starts, rootfs fails | fstab entries, encryption (FBE), SELinux | inspect `dmesg` for mount errors, check `cryptsetup`/`fscrypt` support |
| Wi-Fi missing | no vendor firmware or no mainline driver | use `firmware` blobs from the vendor GPL release, load with `modprobe` |
| Antenna/modem dead | calibration partitions were overwritten | restore `persist`/`efs`/`nvdata` from the backup; never flash the `modem` partition |

## 4. Slot, dynamic partitions and persistence

- A/B devices: `fastboot flash boot --slot _a` and `--slot _b`; check
  `fastboot getvar current-slot` and `ro.boot.slot_suffix`. After flashing, verify
  the other slot still holds a working image: `fastboot set_active` is Tier 2.
- Dynamic partitions (`super`): a custom OS that does not use `super` needs the
  vendor `super.img` to stay intact for OTA/rollback. Prefer installing to `userdata`
  or a dedicated partition, or accept losing OTA updates.
- `vbmeta`: flashing `vbmeta` with `--disable-verity --disable-verification` is the
  standard entry point for custom kernels. It is Tier 2 and it weakens the
  verified boot chain: state the consequences.
- Re-locking the bootloader with a custom OS can permanently brick the device. Do
  not suggest it (`references/safety.md`).

## 5. Package structure (postmarketOS)

```
device-<vendor>-<codename>/
  APKBUILD            # metadata, depends, install scripts
  deviceinfo          # board description used to build the boot image
  init-boot.sh        # first-boot tweaks, fstab, firmware loading
linux-<vendor>-<codename>/
  APKBUILD            # kernel package: source, config, patches
  config             # kernel configuration (or config fragment + defaults)
  patches/            # out-of-tree patches
```

- `deviceinfo` keys that matter: `name`, `manufacturer`, `codename`, `arch`,
  `arch64`, `qemu`, `flash_method`, `bootimg_header_version`, `page_size`,
  `cmdline`, `dtb`, `deviceinfo_generate_bootimg`, `fdt`, `allowed_unsafe_access`.
- Test the metadata before building: `pmbootstrap kconfig check` and
  `pmbootstrap kconfig merge` (kernel config), `pmbootstrap build --dry-run`? (the
  build itself is `pmbootstrap build`).
- Keep the kernel in version control, one commit per functional change, and keep
  the patches minimal enough to be upstreamable.

## 6. Definition of done for a port

- Boots reliably to a shell over USB with the stock `fastboot` (RAM) image.
- Boots persistently from a slot, survives a reboot, and can be restored with the
  stock boot image.
- Display, touch, storage and network are documented as working.
- The status table is complete and honest about what is broken.
- The device page on the postmarketOS wiki is updated (or a patch is prepared).

# Safety reference

## Before any write to a device
- Battery above 60%, original cable, no hubs, stable host (no sleep/suspend).
- Identify the exact model + region variant. Firmware for a sibling model is the classic way to brick.
- Know the recovery path BEFORE flashing: fastboot recovery, Odin/download mode, Qualcomm EDL (9008), MediaTek BROM/preloader (SP Flash Tool / mtkclient), Rockchip maskrom, Pixel/Google factory images.
- Unlocking the bootloader usually wipes /data. Say so and confirm the user's data is backed up.
- Calibration partitions (persist, efs, modemst1/2, nvdata/nvram, proinfo, protect_f/s) are device-unique and are not in any firmware package. Back them up first when possible.

## Pre-flight checklist (run before every Tier 2 command)
1. `fastboot devices` / `adb devices` shows exactly the intended device.
2. Battery > 60% and the cable is stable.
3. The exact firmware/image file was hashed (`sha256sum`) and the hash recorded.
4. The stock image for the current slot is backed up and verified.
5. The device-unique calibration partitions are backed up, or the user explicitly accepted the risk.
6. The recovery path for this exact model is known and reachable.
7. Anti-rollback was checked (`fastboot getvar anti`, vbmeta rollback index): the image to flash is not older than what is installed.
8. The user saw the flash-gate checklist and answered "yes" to that exact command.

## Anti-rollback and verified boot
- Many vendors (Xiaomi, Samsung, Oppo/OnePlus, Google, Qualcomm devices with rollback index) refuse older bootloaders/firmware and can hard-brick. Never flash an older bootloader/firmware than installed without checking the rollback index (`fastboot getvar anti`, vbmeta rollback_index, vendor docs).
- vbmeta: flashing with `--disable-verity --disable-verification` is a Tier 2 action; state why.
- Re-locking the bootloader with a non-stock OS can brick. Do not suggest it.

## Vendor notes (verify with current docs; policies change)
- Samsung: Odin/download mode, KG/RMM state (can block unlock for a week or permanently), Knox eFuse trips irreversibly.
- Xiaomi: Mi Unlock account + waiting period; anti-rollback (`anti` var); fastbootd vs fastboot.
- Pixel/OnePlus: `fastboot flashing unlock`; A/B slots; flash both slots consciously.
- MediaTek: preloader corruption = no fastboot; need BROM tools and a donor preloader.
- Qualcomm: EDL needs a signed firehose loader on many newer models; keep stock firehose if available.
- Carrier-locked / enterprise-managed (MDM) / FRP-locked devices: do not attempt bypasses. Ask for proof of ownership context; refuse circumvention of theft protections (FRP, activation lock, IMEI changes).

## Recovery paths by platform

| Platform | Emergency path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Qualcomm | EDL 9008 + firehose loader | Loader is model-specific and vendor-signed; keep a copy of the stock one |
| MediaTek | BROM (preloader absent) / DA mode | `mtkclient` can read calibration and write in BROM |
| Samsung | Odin download mode | Needs the exact model/region firmware |
| Rockchip | Maskrom / Loader | Requires the vendor loader and rkdeveloptool |
| Exynos | Download mode | Vendor tools only |
| AOSP/Google | `fastboot flashing unlock` + factory images | Factory images are region-locked; check the model suffix |

If no recovery path is confirmed for the exact model, do not perform Tier 2 or 3
actions. State the risk and let the user decide with full information.

## Forbidden by default (Tier 3)
`fastboot erase *`, `fastboot format *`, `fastboot flash` of bootloader/aboot/abl/xbl/sbl/tz/hyp/modem/radio/preloader/persist/efs/nvram, `dd of=/dev/block/*`, anything that changes IMEI/serial/baseband identity, `flashing lock` on custom OS.

Also forbidden: FRP/activation-lock bypass, IMEI/serial modification, baseband identity
changes, and defeating carrier locks. These are theft protections, not obstacles to
"unlock a phone".

## When the user insists on a Tier 3 action
1. Restate the concrete risk: what bricks, what is unrecoverable, which eFuse trips.
2. Show the recovery path, or state that there is none.
3. Require an explicit, informed override in the conversation.
4. If the action is an anti-theft bypass rather than a technical risk, refuse.

## Reporting
Always list: what was changed, how to revert, what could not be reverted (eFuse, rollback counters, data wipe).
Never include serials, IMEIs or MAC addresses in the report; use the device hash.

# Tooling

What each tool does, which tier it belongs to and how to install it.
`bash scripts/setup-host.sh --check` prints the status of all of them on this host;
`--full` installs everything that is missing.

## Core (required)

| Tool | Purpose | Tier | Install |
|---|---|---|---|
| `adb` | device shell, properties, logcat, pull/push, sideload | 0–2 | `apt install adb` / `dnf install android-tools` / `pacman -S android-tools` / `brew install --cask android-platform-tools` |
| `fastboot` | bootloader protocol: `getvar`, `boot`, `flash`, `flashing unlock` | 0–2 | same package as `adb` |
| `python3` | runs the bundled parsers | 0 | everywhere |

## Analysis

| Tool | Purpose | Install |
|---|---|---|
| `dtc` | compile/decompile device trees (`dtc -I dtb -O dts`) | `apt install device-tree-compiler` / `dnf install dtc` / `pacman -S dtc` / `brew install dtc` |
| `unpack_bootimg` | split a boot image into kernel/ramdisk/dtb (AOSP `mkbootimg`) | not packaged by most distros: build from AOSP `platform/tools/mkbootimg`, use the `osm0sis/bootimg` release, or rely on the bundled `scripts/lib/bootimg.py` |
| `scripts/lib/bootimg.py` | bundled dependency-free boot image parser (header, cmdline, dtb extraction) | already here |
| `avbtool` | vbmeta inspection: rollback index, flags, chained descriptors | `pipx install "avbtool @ git+https://github.com/google/avb"` |
| `payload-dumper-go` | extract partitions from an A/B OTA `payload.bin` | GitHub release binary (the setup script fetches the latest release asset) |
| `simg2img` | convert Android sparse images to raw | `apt install android-sdk-libsparse-utils` or the `anestisb/android-image-tools` release |
| `lpunpack` | split `super.img` into its logical partitions | `apt install android-sdk-ext4-utils`? not packaged: `AndroidDumps/Ext4Extractor` release, or build from AOSP `system/extras` |
| `fsck.erofs` | read EROFS images read-only | `apt install erofs-utils` / `dnf install erofs-utils` |
| `e2fsck`/`debugfs` | read ext4 images read-only | `apt install e2fsprogs` |
| `lz4` | decompress Samsung/MTK firmware members | `apt install lz4` |
| `unzip`, `7z`, `file`, `strings` | open and identify vendor packages | `apt install unzip p7zip-full file binutils` |
| `binwalk` | signature scan of firmware (optional) | `pipx install binwalk` |

## Porting

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pmbootstrap` | build and flash postmarketOS | `pipx install pmbootstrap`; needs `sudo` for the chroot, `qemu-user-static` for foreign architectures |
| `git`, `curl` | fetch kernels, DTS and the pmOS port recipes | `apt install git curl` |
| `dtc` + `fdtget` | device tree work | as above |

## Recovery (expert, use only on a device you own)

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `mtkclient` | MediaTek BROM/DA mode, preloader, partition read/write | `pipx install mtkclient`; `mtk rca` (read calibration), `mtk download` (write) |
| EDL / firehose loader | Qualcomm emergency download mode | The loader is vendor-signed per model; use only the one matching your device, and only for your own device |
| Odin | Samsung download mode (Windows) | Samsung firmware must match the exact model/region |
| SP Flash Tool | MediaTek scatter-file flashing (Windows) | Needs the vendor preloader and scatter file |

## Minimal host checklist

`adb`, `fastboot`, `python3`, `dtc`, `unzip`, `strings`, `file`, `jq`, `git`, `curl`.
Everything else is optional and only unlocks deeper analysis.

## Rules

- Prefer the packaged tool over a random binary from a forum. If you download one,
  record its sha256 and compare it with the release's published checksum.
- Never run a binary extracted from a firmware package. Analyse it, list it, hash it.
- Keep the host toolchain and the device toolchain (`adb`/`fastboot`) in sync with
  the platform-tools version the vendor expects when a command fails oddly.
